title: Your emergency fund: how much you really need

lines.text: A car repair or a lost job shouldn't turn into credit card debt. That's what an emergency fund is for.
A common goal is three to six months of essential expenses.
lines.say: A common goal is three to six months of essential expenses.

lines.text: If your essentials cost twenty-five hundred a month, that's seventy-five hundred to fifteen thousand dollars.
lines.say: If your essentials cost twenty-five hundred a month, that's seventy-five hundred, to fifteen thousand dollars.

lines.text: That sounds like a lot, so start small. A first goal of five hundred dollars already covers many surprise bills.
Automate it. Even twenty-five dollars every payday adds up, and keep it in a separate savings account so you don't spend it.

scene.headline: [Automate] it. Keep it separate.
scene.sub: A high-yield savings account works well

lines.text: And only use it for real emergencies. A sale is not an emergency.
That's the money. See you at the next bell.
